maria: Running into a funky combo when bootstrapping the sample worker app with the TS SDK. Edge runtime throws and types are weird. Anyone seen this?
leo: What error at runtime? ESM vs CJS?
maria: Wrangler runtime error: "Uncaught SyntaxError: Cannot use import statement outside a module". In TS, autocomplete shows client.call(...) as 'any' unless I force a generic.
kai: Sounds like your bundler resolved the CJS entrypoint. Which SDK import are you using?
maria: import { createClient } from '@redwood-inference/js-sdk';
jen: Two things to check: package.json "exports" and tsconfig moduleResolution. Some bundlers (esbuild/vite) treat node resolution differently and pick require path.
leo: Also check package published types. If types point to a single index.d.ts that re-exports CJS shapes with overloads that return unknown, TS inference collapses.
maria: Here's my tsconfig: ```json { "compilerOptions": { "target": "ES2021", "module": "ESNext", "moduleResolution": "node", "esModuleInterop": true, "skipLibCheck": true } } ```
kai: Change moduleResolution to "bundler" or "node16" depending on your toolchain. For Wrangler/vite, "bundler" usually works. Also set "preserveValueImports": false? (depends).
jen: Quick hack: annotate call sites with generics like `await client.call<MyType>(...)` but we should avoid forcing everyone.
leo: For a proper SDK fix we can: 1) ensure exports map has explicit "import" path to esm, 2) publish separate worker entrypoint, 3) update d.ts so overloads favor a default generic and don't widen to unknown/any.
maria: Example exports suggestion you can publish: ```json "exports": { "./": { "import": "./dist/esm/index.mjs", "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js", "types": "./dist/index.d.ts" }, "./worker": { "import": "./dist/esm/worker-entry.mjs", "types": "./dist/worker.d.ts" } } ```
jen: Also consider adding "typesVersions" to package.json so TS resolves different d.ts for older TS targets or cjs consumers. Something like: ```json "typesVersions": { "*": { "*": [ "dist/types/*" ] } } ```
kai: Another gotcha: if the public d.ts uses overloads like `call<T = unknown>(...): Promise<T>` and then a fallback overload returns `any`, inference becomes garbage. We should prefer a single generic signature `call<T = unknown>(opts: CallOpts): Promise<T>` and keep helper overloads minimal.
leo: We should also update the sample worker repo to include a minimal tsconfig for edge: ```json { "compilerOptions": { "module": "ESNext", "moduleResolution": "bundler", "target": "ES2021", "allowSyntheticDefaultImports": true, "skipLibCheck": true } } ```
maria: Tried that. Switching to moduleResolution:"bundler" + adding package export for ./worker fixed runtime. Types improved but still needed one call-site generic to get full structure.
jen: Could be our generics defaulting to unknown. We can change default generic to Record<string, any> or a library-specific JsonValue to make inference usable without annotation. Open to bikeshedding that.
kai: I propose: default generic = JsonValue, single exported signature, avoid multiple overlapping overloads. Also add a small augmenting declaration in dist/types/compat.d.ts to help older TS.
leo: I'll sketch a PR: - change index.d.ts to a single generic signature - add worker export entry - add typesVersions for compatibility - update README with edge/ts troubleshooting
jen: Add a short onboarding FAQ in sample-app README: "Edge Workers: if you see import syntax errors, ensure moduleResolution:bundler and use `import { createClient } from '@redwood-inference/js-sdk/worker'`".
ci-bot: CI: edge-integration job failed yesterday, created ticket #705 assigned to @eng-runtime.
maria: Thanks y'all, that unblocked the sample app. I'll paste the minimal diff for onboarding.
maria: Diff: ```diff package.json {+ "exports": {+ "./": { "import": "./dist/esm/index.mjs", "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js", "types": "./dist/index.d.ts" },+ "./worker": { "import": "./dist/esm/worker-entry.mjs", "types": "./dist/worker.d.ts" }+ } } ``` and tsconfig snippet: ```diff { "compilerOptions": { - "moduleResolution": "node" + "moduleResolution": "bundler", + "allowSyntheticDefaultImports": true } } ```
jen: Perfect, I'll add to onboarding docs and the sample worker README.
kai: Reminder: add a unit test that loads the package via esbuild with worker target to catch regressed exports.
leo: Filed issues: #706 (types overload cleanup), #707 (worker export), #708 (sample-app onboarding).
maria: Great. Ship the PRs and ping devex to update docs. :party_parrot:
